chunks: Some of our companions wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding the endowment (waqf) and what is reported about it, so he (peace be upon him) wrote: The endowment stands according to what its owners dedicate it for, if Allah wills.

key_terms.إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ: If Allah wills (a common closing formula indicating divine permission)
key_terms.الْوَقْفِ: Endowment (waqf), a permanent dedication of property for religious or charitable purposes
key_terms.فَوَقَّعَ: He wrote/inscribed (referring to the Imam's written reply)

ai.seo_question: What determines the validity and conditions of an Islamic endowment (waqf) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise ruling from Imam al-Hadi (AS), the autonomy of the donor (waqif) is affirmed, establishing that the specific conditions set by the owner govern the endowment's execution. This principle underscores the flexibility of waqf in Shia jurisprudence, allowing for diverse stipulations regarding usage, beneficiaries, and duration, provided they do not contradict Sharia. It reflects the broader Islamic legal maxim that the donor's intent is paramount in charitable dedications.

en.hubeali: ‘Some of our companions wrote to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> regarding the dedication and what is reported with regards to it. (He<sup>asws</sup>) said: ‘The dedication depends upon the what (stipulation) its owner has dedicated with, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.
en.sarwar: 34. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated the following:

“Certain persons of our people had written to abu Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about endowment and what is narrated about it. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, signed the answer that said, ‘An endowment is according to what people making the endowment do (condition they set), by the will of Allah.”’
